storyline.latest_title: How Cursor knew Claude Fable 5 was ready for the hardest 1% of problems | Claude by Anthropic

prior_narrative.tldr: SonarQube extended its trusted-verification plugins to cover Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, and Cursor on Jul 1. A week later a Datadog engineer published a detailed account of pairing Claude and Cursor for a real production storage migration.
prior_narrative.whats_new: MarkTechPost scored four coding agents — Mistral Vibe for Code, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex — on the same scaffold-to-PR task on Jul 14, giving builders a like-for-like comparison instead of vendor benchmarks.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Coding-agent choice is becoming an evaluable decision: cross-agent verification tooling and apples-to-apples task benchmarks now exist, so teams no longer have to take vendor performance claims on faith.

status.detail: Coverage keeps pairing Claude Code and Cursor as both production tools and benchmark subjects rather than settling on one winner.

beats.headline: SonarQube extends trusted-verification plugins to Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, and Cursor
beats.summary: One verification layer now spans the major coding agents instead of being tied to a single vendor.

beats.headline: Datadog engineer details pairing Claude and Cursor for a production storage migration
beats.summary: A test-driven migration account shares what worked and what didn't running the two agents together against a real production system.

beats.headline: MarkTechPost scores Mistral Vibe for Code, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex on one scaffold-to-PR task
beats.summary: Four agents run the same task on the same scaffold, producing a directly comparable score instead of separate vendor claims.

open_questions: Does the MarkTechPost scaffold-to-PR scoring hold up under independent replication with different tasks?
Do cross-agent verification plugins like SonarQube's catch real logic bugs, or only style and formatting differences?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Before standardizing on one coding agent, run the same scaffold-to-PR task through your shortlist yourself, and check whether your review tooling already verifies that agent's output rather than assuming vendor benchmarks transfer to your codebase.
